assessment: Six of these ten answer something the audit measured: the graveyard class no card in the 99 covers, a blue count five sources under Karsten's 90% figure, and an interaction suite the diagnosis calls wide and slow. Three widen the kill itself — the verified Aetherflux Reservoir line assembles in 0.7% of games and rests on one creature, and Teferi, Time Raveler and Tidespout Tyrant are the only cards in this identity that hand the Reservoir a second engine. Black Vise takes the punisher half from six copies to seven, moving it from 36.4% of openers to the corpus's cited 41%, and Windfall is the card that makes those punishers hit for their maximum on a turn you choose. Narset, Parter of Veils is deliberately absent: capping opponents at one draw a turn also empties the hands Iron Maiden and Ebony Owl Netsuke bill.

combo_lines_opened.produces: Near-infinite storm count, near-infinite colourless mana and card draw

ten.closes: engine component: Hullbreaker Horror (the verified kill's only irreplaceable card)
ten.why: Displacer Kitten and Sol Ring are already in the 99, so this is the one three-mana card that offers Aetherflux Reservoir an engine that does not run through a seven-mana creature — and its static line stops the pod answering your commit turn at instant speed, which is the exact window stack 006 says the Horror leaves open.
ten.unlocks: A second route to the Reservoir ledger, and a turn where three opponents' held counterspells and removal are sorcery-speed only.

ten.why: The card-advantage liability is that 22 copies of draw feed four seats, not one; a turn-one Sentinel taxes the first noncreature spell each opponent casts every turn, and a deck that gives three players extra cards is a deck those players cast more spells from.
ten.unlocks: A draw slot that only ever draws for you, live from turn one and fetchable with Enlightened Tutor as an artifact.

ten.closes: engine component: the draw punisher group (6 cards — thinnest component of the core two-piece target)
ten.why: One mana for Iron Maiden's exact upkeep clock aimed at one seat, taking the punisher half from six copies to seven — the corpus prices that step exactly: "5 copies is 31% of openers, 7 is 41% (WitchPHD's 7-of, the singleton 4-of, 41.1%), 10 is 54%".
ten.unlocks: A turn-one punisher, so the turn-two Howling Mine is a plan rather than a donation; Enlightened Tutor reaches it because it is an artifact.

combo_lines_opened.produces: Infinite colourless mana, infinite storm count

ten.closes: engine component: Hullbreaker Horror (the verified kill's only irreplaceable card)
ten.why: It is the only other card in blue and white that does the Horror's job — a cast trigger that bounces a permanent — so the kill's class stops having exactly one member and a mulligan can look for two cards instead of one.
ten.unlocks: A second body the Reservoir ledger can run on, at the cost of one more mana and the Horror's uncounterable line.

ten.why: Three no-maximum-hand-size effects let this deck hoard, and Windfall turns that hoard into three refilled hands for three mana at a moment you pick — cast it in your second main with Iron Maiden and Ebony Owl Netsuke already down and every opponent walks into their upkeep holding your hand size.
ten.unlocks: A scheduled punisher turn instead of a hoped-for one; the honest cost is that your held Fierce Guardianship goes with it.

ten.why: Graveyard is the one class of the five that no card in the 99 answers, and this deck hands a reanimator or a delve pilot extra cards every turn cycle; the sacrifice mode exiles each opponent's graveyard only, so Torrential Gearhulk and Dig Through Time keep working where Rest in Peace would blank both.
ten.unlocks: The fifth interaction class for one mana, with a {1}-and-sacrifice draw mode in the matchups that do not want it.

ten.why: Blue sits at 31 sources against Karsten's 36 and white at 20 against 22, which is what makes a turn-two Counterspell hold or a turn-two Kami of the Crescent Moon a coin-flip; one untapped card that is literally a Plains and an Island moves both counts, and Flooded Strand is already in the 99 to fetch it.
ten.unlocks: A double-pip curve — Counterspell, Force of Negation, Grand Abolisher, Supreme Verdict — that casts on time more often, without adding to the two taplands.

ten.why: The suite is wide and slow: only Swords to Plowshares and Path to Exile answer a resolved permanent cheaply and both are creature-only, so a resolved Rhystic Study or an opposing Aetherflux Reservoir has no cheap answer at all — March exiles an artifact, creature or enchantment at instant speed and scales with the mana you did not spend.
ten.unlocks: An instant-speed answer to the three permanent classes counterspells only cover on the way in, castable on the same turn you hold up interaction.

combo_lines_opened.produces: Infinite colourless mana, infinite storm count

ten.why: This one answers a measured rate rather than a named axis: the kill assembles in 0.7% of games and 0.3% by turn six, its cheap-rock component holds exactly two cards, and Mana Vault is the rock whose arithmetic differs from the pair stack 004 settled at exactly mana-neutral — cast for {1}, taps for three.
ten.unlocks: A third recastable rock for the loop, and the question of whether the ledger becomes mana-positive rather than merely unbounded in casts.

ten.closes: engine component: Hullbreaker Horror (the verified kill's only irreplaceable card)
ten.why: Eight counterspells cover everything except a removal spell aimed at the Horror on the turn you tapped out for seven mana, and stack 006 says out loud that the loop's own priority windows give you no protection — equip {0} puts shroud on it the turn it lands.
ten.unlocks: A commit turn that survives targeted removal; it does not answer Supreme Verdict, an edict, or a sweeper, and shroud stops your own targeting too.

gaps: Mana Vault's ledger is unsettled. Stack 004 proved the Sol Ring plus Arcane Signet loop is exactly mana-neutral; whether substituting a rock that costs {1} and taps for three makes it positive is a /resolve-stack question. The combo database's two-card Hullbreaker Horror plus Mana Vault claim is the same shape stack 001 refuted, so it should not be read as a shortcut.

Tidespout Tyrant's trigger is mandatory and must target a permanent, where the Horror's is 'choose up to one'. Whether the alternating-rock loop reproduces under a forced target — or is compelled to bounce your own lands — needs its own scenario before the redundancy claim is priced.

Teferi, Time Raveler plus Displacer Kitten plus Sol Ring is a popular database line, and stack 005 already found that the Kitten's blink and the Horror's bounce cannot both resolve usefully on one cast. Whether blinking a planeswalker to reset its loyalty loops here is unresolved.

Braingeyser, Mathemagics, Prosperity and Skyscribing are the deck's on-demand hand-fillers, and each is priced against its own pick rather than as a set; taking all four leaves Stroke of Genius, Folio of Fancies, Temple Bell and Windfall to push an opponent past Iron Maiden's four cards and Ebony Owl Netsuke's seven.

Alms Collector is the strongest white answer to a symmetric-draw deck's own gift and is off this list on a rules question, not a deckbuilding one: whether 'if an opponent would draw two or more cards' applies to Howling Mine's additional draw-step card. A stack scenario would settle it and could earn it a slot.
No deck_recon.json exists for this deck, so none of these ten is weighed against what strong lists for this commander actually run — only against this deck's own measurements and the strategy corpus.
